{{Quotation |Things never to do in an OS #1: {{nested|template}} triple-fault here we come |Kemp }}
==Causes== If a fault occurs while invoking the double fault handler, the system reboots with a triple fault. See [[Interrupt Descriptor Table#Gate Descriptor|the IDT]] and [[Nonexistent Page]].
Note that a fault that occurs while a fault handler is already running does not of itself cause a double or triple fault. For example, if a Segment Not Present Fault occurs while a page fault handler is running, the CPU simply invokes the segment not present handler. Only a fault raised during the delivery of an exception - while the CPU is reading the IDT entry, loading the code segment, or pushing the exception frame onto the stack - counts towards a double fault. The most common cause in a hobby kernel is an IDT that was never loaded, or one whose entries point at a code selector that does not exist in the GDT.
==Avoiding== Use a separate [[Task State Segment|TSS]] for double faults.

The Programmable Interval Timer chip (Intel 8253/8254) is an oscillator, a prescaler and 3 independent frequency dividers. The timer can raise IRQ 0.
== I/O Ports == Channel 0 data port is 0x40.
The APIC timer is calibrated against the PIT or the TSC. Unlike the timer chip, it is per-CPU. See [[PIT]].
